articles.title: China says will safeguard its own interests as US expands Iran sanctions
articles.summary: China has advocated for a ceasefire, insisting US sanctions will not resolve the Middle East conflict.
articles.body:
China has said that it would safeguard its interests after Washington unveiled new measures while laying out plans for the “economic asphyxiation” of Beijing’s economic partner Iran.

Speaking at a regular news briefing in Beijing on Tuesday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian rejected Washington’s expanding pressure campaign, calling for an immediate end to unilateral measures.

list 1 of 3 How US sanctions on Iran ripple through global markets and consumers

list 2 of 3 The Iran war is bringing cyberwarfare into critical infrastructure

list 3 of 3 Can Pakistani army chief make Iran’s military leaders restart US talks?

“Cooperation between China and Iran has always been conducted within the framework of international law and should not be interfered with or disrupted,” Lin said.

“China has already stated many times that it firmly opposes illegal unilateral sanctions … China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights and interests.”

The latest comments come nearly six months into the US-Israel war on Iran, as the United States rolls out new penalties on entities including several in China.

Washington also expanded secondary sanctions threats, urging governments worldwide to join its economic campaign.

Asked on Monday whether Chinese banks would be targeted by the new penalties, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said, “No one is above the reach of US sanctions.”

China has advocated for a ceasefire, insisting US sanctions will not resolve the conflict.

Beijing remains a key customer for Iranian oil and is directly affected by the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran has weathered sanctions for decades, using complex international financial networks to evade restrictions. Before the war, it continued to export millions of barrels of oil, mostly to China.

‘We will see a lot of resistance’ from China

Amid the US’s latest move, some analysts say threats to sanction Chinese entities over trade with Iran are unlikely to materialise. This is due to a combination of diplomatic and legal obstacles, according to Trita Parsi, executive vice president of the Washington-based Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft.

“If the US now goes after the Chinese only weeks before [Chinese President] Xi [Jinping] is supposed to arrive in Washington, I find it unlikely,” Parsi told Al Jazeera, pointing out that Washington faces significant friction on both fronts.

Diplomatically, Parsi pointed out that Beijing helped avert a severe economic crisis during the height of the war by halting its oil purchases just as prices spiked, cratering demand and keeping crude under $100 per barrel for extended periods.

“They did this because the Chinese objective was to make sure this crisis would not bring about a global recession, which would be bad for China,” Parsi said, suggesting the move indirectly spared Washington from an energy shock that would have hurt the US economy.

Beyond that, Beijing is unlikely to accept US attacks on its companies or economic interests without pushback. “I suspect that we will see a lot of resistance from the Chinese if the US actually ends up going after Chinese companies,” Parsi said.

Separately, the president of the Iran-China Chamber of Commerce and Industries, Majidreza Hariri, also criticised US policies, warning that Washington has entered into an economic war with Tehran.

“What Trump has said makes it clear that he has entered into an economic war with us and considers it a new phase of military and security wars!” Hariri wrote in a post on X.

“With this same reasoning, all of America’s economic targets and its partners around the world, and especially in the region, are considered military targets of the enemy and are targetable!”

articles.title: Vanguard strategist says retirees need 'a complete mind shift' — and shares 4 principles to ease financial anxiety
articles.summary: A retirement nest egg is only useful if you’re comfortable spending it. Here’s how experts say retirees can balance lasting financial security while actually...
articles.body:
Moneywise and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue through links in the content below.

From travelling the world to embracing a second act to simply hitting the hammock in your own backyard, everyone has a different retirement fantasy.

But for many, once they've walked away from work, that fantasy gives way to the anxiety-riddled reality of living the rest of their lives without a steady income.

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

JPMorgan sees gold hitting $5,000/oz by Q4 — and savvy investors are protecting their wealth with a tax-advantaged Gold IRA. Get your free guide from Priority Gold

The tax breaks in Trump's 'big beautiful bill' expire after 2028. Here are 4 moves to make before the window closes

"Moving from a saving mindset to a spending mindset is really difficult for most people," Garrett Harbron, Head of Advised Wealth Management Strategies at Vanguard, told Moneywise. After decades of diligent saving, he added, watching that bank account balance drop instead of rise can be stress-inducing.

And retirement income anxiety begins long before that final work whistle blows. An April Gallup poll found that 62% of Americans stress that they haven't accumulated enough retirement savings, while 54% worry about maintaining their lifestyle (1).

"This causes some retirees to spend less than they can actually afford in retirement and maybe not live the life they'd really like to," he added. "That's why starting with purpose is so important."

As such, Harbron, who noted the shift in focus requires "a complete mind shift" in an interview with CBS (2), helped outline some strategies for doing just that as the lead researcher for Vanguard's Principles for Retirement Income (3), which offers four key principles for mindful money management — and subsequent stress relief.

The four principles for retirement financial security

From dynamic spending to adhering to the 4% rule, everyone has a different take on how to handle retirement income.

Harbron said Vanguard's four principles "ensure that retirees know what they want their retirement to be, how they will spend their money, have security knowing that their money will last and the time to enjoy their retirement."

Harbron said this first step is "about setting goals, creating a spending plan, ensuring it's sustainable and thinking about the risks that might knock your plan off track." He called it "the foundation of any successful retirement plan."

articles.title: 'A whole new vibe': Ashwini Vaishnaw shares glimpse of bullet train project taking shape
articles.summary: India Business News: Indiaâs first bullet train is slowly moving from plans to pillars. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Tuesday shared a glimpse of the work taking sh.
articles.body: Indiaâs first bullet train is slowly moving from plans to pillars. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Tuesday shared a glimpse of the work taking shape across Thane and Palghar, calling it, "a whole new vibe!" The 135.45-km elevated section stretches from Shilphata in Thane district to Zaroli village on the Maharashtra-Gujarat border.The route cuts through varied terrain, with 124.027 km of the section comprising viaducts and bridges, the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) said in an official release on Tuesday.The construction is at different stages along the stretch. Pier work is underway across more than 100 km, while nearly 74 km of piers have been completed and are ready for viaduct girders.The work is being supported by nine casting yards, seven full-span launching gantries and eight SBS launching gantries, all currently operational in Maharashtra.Three elevated stations are also coming up along the stretch: Thane, Virar and Boisar. The Thane station has a concourse level around 12 metres above the natural ground level, a design aimed at protecting and preserving local mangroves in the eco-sensitive zone.The tunnels are making progress too. Of the seven planned mountain tunnels on the section, three have already achieved breakthrough, with drainage, waterproofing and lining work now underway.Bridges are another key part of the stretch, including a 460-metre bridge over the Ulhas River, a 2.32-km bridge over the Vaitarna River and a 510-metre bridge over the Jagani River.Overall, the section will have 36 bridges and crossings, including 12 steel bridges over major railway lines, the Mumbai-Nashik Highway and the Ulhas River.The release said the progress reflects the engineering work behind the project under Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs vision and Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnawâs drive to expand next-generation railway infrastructure.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Gold's rally just hit a wall — how to play a tactical pullback with limited risk: Alpha Options Playbook
articles.summary: Gold may have gotten ahead of itself for now. It's pausing after rallying into a key technical level, getting stretched to the upside in the process.
articles.body:
Gold ( GC=F ) may have gotten ahead of itself for now. It's pausing after rallying into a key technical level, getting stretched to the upside in the process.

SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ) ripped higher from its July low, part of a broader gold breakout that is repairing much of the damage from earlier this year.

The bigger recovery still looks intact. The near-term setup is a different story.

GLD topped out near $496 earlier this year before sliding to a July closing low of about $365. Halfway between those two levels sits $430.

That is almost exactly where buyers ran out of gas on Monday.

GLD traded just short of that level Monday before opening lower Tuesday. The rally had also become technically overbought — having traveled too far too fast — giving sellers another reason to show up around a level that was already important on the chart.

Last week, the iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) rallied almost exactly halfway back from its June-to-July plunge , hit resistance, and rolled over.

Now gold is taking a run at the same playbook.

The next area to watch is around $415. That is near the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement of GLD's decline and also close to its 200-day moving average.

Fundstrat global head of technical strategy Mark Newton sees room for a pause without abandoning the bigger bullish case.

"I sense that gold as well as cryptocurrencies likely [are] going to back and fill a little bit. We'll see some consolidation in the month of September," Newton told Yahoo Finance on Monday (video above). "Ultimately, it's going to be great to buy dips."

That gives us a downside target. It also gives us an options trade.

The first leg is buying one Sept. 25 $425 put.

That put gains value as GLD falls, but buying it alone means paying for downside well beyond the $415 area we are targeting.

Selling one Sept. 25 $415 put helps offset that cost.

Together, the two options create a $425/$415 bear put spread for a net debit of about $4.60, or $460 per spread.

The maximum loss is the $460 paid upfront. The spread breaks even at $420.40 at expiration.

If GLD finishes at $415 or lower on Sept. 25, the spread reaches its maximum value of $10. That produces a maximum profit of $540, or roughly 117% on the amount at risk.

The trade is built for a pullback, not a collapse.

A quick move back above roughly $430 would weaken the setup. On the downside, $415 is where the chart starts offering support, and where the options trade has already done all the work it can do.

That is why selling the $415 put fits this setup so well. There is little reason to pay for a much deeper sell-off when the technical target sits right there.

That put gains value as GLD falls, but buying it alone means paying for downside well beyond the $415 area we are targeting.
Selling one Sept. 25 $415 put helps offset that cost.
Together, the two options create a $425/$415 bear put spread for a net debit of about $4.60, or $460 per spread.
The maximum loss is the $460 paid upfront. The spread breaks even at $420.40 at expiration.
If GLD finishes at $415 or lower on Sept. 25, the spread reaches its maximum value of $10. That produces a maximum profit of $540, or roughly 117% on the amount at risk.
The trade is built for a pullback, not a collapse.
A quick move back above roughly $430 would weaken the setup. On the downside, $415 is where the chart starts offering support, and where the options trade has already done all the work it can do.
That is why selling the $415 put fits this setup so well. There is little reason to pay for a much deeper sell-off when the technical target sits right there.

articles.title: Canada hits US with counter-tariffs on more than 700 products
articles.summary: Canada imposes tariffs on $19.9bn of US goods which will take effect on September 8 as trade talks with Washington collapse.
articles.body:
Canada has announced retaliatory tariffs against the United States as the trade war between Washington and Ottawa escalates, impacting hundreds of products.

On Tuesday, the Canadian government said it would impose tariffs on 27.6 billion Canadian dollars, or $19.9bn, worth of US goods, matching “dollar for dollar” the new US duties that Trump imposed. It also announced a new plan for financial support for businesses caught in the trade war.

list 2 of 4 Who are Iran’s top trading partners US would need to target to isolate it?

list 3 of 4 How can a heavily indebted football club afford Mo Salah?

list 4 of 4 China says will safeguard its own interests as US expands Iran sanctions

The counter-tariffs will impact more than 700 products, the government said in a statement, and will target the steel and aluminium, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, plastics and electronics sectors.

The tariffs will range from 15 percent to 50 percent and take effect on September 8.

The Canadian government also announced a new 7.5 billion-Canadian-dollar ($5.42bn) funding package to help small- and medium-sized businesses mitigate financial risks caused by the new tariffs.

The new tariffs come after US President Donald Trump imposed 50 percent tariffs on Canadian products on Saturday, impacting $20bn worth of Canadian goods, only days after announcing a deal.

On Monday, Trump announced new tariffs on Canadian autos , which would double existing tariffs to 50 percent from January 1.

Trump has also hurled insults at Canada in recent days. On Tuesday, Trump said that he was considering renaming Lake Ontario – the easternmost of the Great Lakes, which borders the Canadian province of Ontario – “Lake America” . The US president also referred to Prime Minister Mark Carney as “Governor Carney”, echoing longstanding remarks about annexing Canada as the “51st state”.

On Tuesday, Trump claimed in a post on Truth Social that the US lost $60bn to Canada annually for the last decade.

But Canada maintains a trade surplus with the US of 9.9 billion Canadian dollars ($7.1bn), according to Statistics Canada. Al Jazeera reached out to the White House for clarification but did not receive a response.

The impact of US tariffs is expected to be felt by US businesses and consumers. Cars and auto parts have been exempt from the tariffs that were imposed on Saturday, but have been a point of contention between Washington and Ottawa.

Canada is the largest purchaser of US-made cars, which could put pressure on American carmakers who rely on Canadian demand.

Meanwhile, US households could face higher prices on 550 consumer goods imported from Canada because of Trump’s 50 percent tariff. Those products include ice skates, toilet paper, some alcoholic beverages and paint.

That could drastically affect Americans, according to a report from the Kiel Institute for the World Economy, an economic think tank, which found that US importers and consumers absorb 96 percent of the tariff burden.

The price of gold, which is largely considered a safe investment in times of economic uncertainty, is trending upwards after falling nearly 1 percent earlier on Tuesday. It remains largely flat, down only 0.03 percent at $4,696 per ounce.

The US dollar has remained fairly stable, down 0.04 percent on Tuesday to 98.96, while the Canadian dollar index has risen comparably by 0.04 percent to 72.27.

On Wall Street, the Nasdaq is up 0.5 percent, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is flat, and the S&P 500 is up 0.2 percent.

In Toronto, the S&P/TSX Composite Index is up 0.6 percent.

articles.title: La Justicia fija un nuevo criterio sobre el teletrabajo: cuidar de familiares enfermos da derecho a tener la jornada completa en remoto
articles.standfirst: Así lo ha confirmado una nueva sentencia del Tribunal Superior de Navarra (TSJN)
articles.summary: Así lo ha confirmado una nueva sentencia del Tribunal Superior de Navarra (TSJN)
articles.body: En determinadas ocasiones, compaginar la vida laboral con la personal es del todo imposible. Los empleados que tienen personas dependientes a su cargo recuerdan que no pueden pasar ocho horas fuera de casa en una oficina. El Tribunal Superior de Navarra (TSJN) les ha terminado dando la razón con una nueva sentencia. El TSJN ha reconocido a una empleada el derecho a teletrabajar el 100% de la jornada, ya que debe cuidar de su madre enferma. Su progenitora tiene un grado de discapacidad del 65% y ha sido diagnosticada con alzhéimer. Ella ocupa un cargo de ingeniera de software en la empresa desde 2006. Para entender los hechos, hay que trasladarse unos años atrás. Desde que estalló la pandemia de COVID-19, ella y sus compañeros habían estado trabajando en régimen total de teletrabajo. Sin embargo, a partir de mayo de 2025, la empresa solicitó que, al menos, debían ir dos días a la semana de forma presencial por petición oficial del cliente, en este caso, el Gobierno de Navarra. Tras esta decisión, la empleada decidió demandar a la empresa solicitando volver al 100% del teletrabajo para cuidar de su madre enferma. Además, también pidió una indemnización por daños morales. La Sección de lo Social del Tribunal de Instancia de Pamplona desestimó esta demanda, ya que consideraba que está fundamentada en necesidad organizativas de la empresa, además de disponer ya de tres días de teletrabajo. El TSJN ha revocado el fallo y le ha terminado dando la razón a la empleada. Eso sí, han desestimado la petición de indemnización. Su decisión se basa en que la empresa no habría abierto un proceso de negociación real, tal y como detalla la ley. Aun así, esta sentencia puede ser recurrida en el Tribunal Supremo.

articles.title: SpaceX unveils Starbase launch site in Louisiana, moves up orbital data center launch timeline
articles.summary: Elon Musk is doing what he always does: making aggressive capex moves and pushing up timelines. SpaceX on Tuesday announced Starbase, Louisiana, a "high cade...
articles.body:
Elon Musk is doing what he always does: making aggressive capex moves and pushing up timelines.

SpaceX ( SPCX ) on Tuesday announced Starbase, Louisiana , a "high cadence" launch site in Louisiana, for its Starship rocket to haul up cargo like the company's Starlink satellites and orbital data centers. SpaceX said Starbase will eventually be able to support "thousands" of Starship launches per year, targeting Earth's orbit, the moon, and Mars.

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said SpaceX will invest $100 billion to build the facility, with construction starting in 2027 and the first Starship launches targeted for 2029. Musk added that Starbase will "ultimately have over a dozen launch towers, enabling more than 30 Starship flights per day."

In addition, the SpaceX CEO took to X to update the timeline for launching the rocket company's first AI-powered satellites, which would eventually depart from Starbase, Louisiana.

"SpaceX, in partnership with Nvidia, has designed a space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 system for launch to orbit in Q4 next year, with significant scale in 2028," Musk said in a post on Monday afternoon.

Musk's post comes on the heels of yesterday's announcement that SpaceX and Nvidia ( NVDA ) would be deploying Nvidia Vera processors "to accelerate the orchestration, code execution, and data processing that powers its next generation of agentic AI."

The companies have worked together in the past and earlier this year announced that Nvidia chips would power SpaceX's upcoming AI satellites , aka orbital data centers.

SpaceX in the past had said it would target 2028 for the launch of these satellites, but Musk's new timeline pulls that forward to Q4 2027, with volume launches in 2028.

Wall Street is positioned for SpaceX to hit these timelines much later and is quite bullish on the prospects.

"From 2029 on, we expect SpaceX to pursue orbital compute towards ~75GW by the end of 2031 at a significantly cheaper cost than could be done on Earth," JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth wrote in a note to clients on Tuesday. "We believe significant upside potential remains as the company quite literally builds out the next frontier."

Musk has been known to issue aggressive timelines that subsequently aren't hit. Look to past timelines for Tesla's Cybertruck, the Tesla Semi, and the still unreleased next-gen Tesla Roadster.

Another key challenge for ramping up orbital data center deployment is how SpaceX will get the payload into space. Its powerful Starship rocket is slated to carry the satellites into space, but it's still in testing.

articles.title: Federal Bank shares fall post merger talks
articles.summary: India Business News: MUMBAI: Shares of Federal Bank closed 3% lower on Tuesday after reports that the lender was pursuing a merger with Jana Small Finance Bank, while Jana.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Shares of Federal Bank closed 3% lower on Tuesday after reports that the lender was pursuing a merger with Jana Small Finance Bank, while Jana SFB fell 2% as sensex closed flat. Both banks later told stock exchanges that they evaluate business opportunities in the ordinary course, without confirming or denying whether merger discussions were underway.Jana Small Finance Bank has sought a universal banking licence from RBI. RBI returned its initial application in June 2025, leaving the lender open to making a future submission.Jana was among the microfinance lenders that received a specialised banking licence in 2017. It began operations as a small finance bank in March and went public in Feb 2024.In its clarification, Federal Bank said it evaluates opportunities for growth and expansion in the ordinary course of business. It said, âthere is no material event/ information that requires disclosure under Regulation 30â of Sebiâs Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements regulations.Jana Small Finance Bank, responding to a request for clarification from BSE and NSE, said it evaluates âall opportunities in the ordinary course of business, from time to timeâ.It said that going ahead, it would continue to make disclosures required under Regulation 30.Get the latest Business News and Live updates.
